items.title: James Hunter interviewed by Monk Rowe, Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018
items.q: But Bob Dylan sort of pretty much broke that with “Like a Rolling Stone” simply because he had a lot to say that couldn’t be contained in that amount of time.

ctx.x: And you don’t wait too long to get to the point.

Yeah I think so. I mean I do like short records. I mean people like Bob Dylan started doing really long ones because, and they used to have to keep it short apparently so that the juke boxes wouldn’t, the album wouldn’t lift up too soon. I think that’s why they were all, up to the early 60s they were all two and a half minutes. But Bob Dylan sort of pretty much broke that with “Like a Rolling Stone” simply because he had a lot to say that couldn’t be contained in that amount of time. And I think by the 80s…
reason records, singles were in excess of four minutes long was because the bulk of the track was the fade out.
